title: Azalea Therapeutics private networking POC kickoff & benchmark scoping
next_steps: Redwood to send VPC peering diagram + PrivateLink checklist
Customer to provide sample inference trace and 1 week token distribution
Schedule 2-week benchmark run window w/ dedicated capacity
action_items: Jordan Miles - send private network diagram, security pack, and cost estimate - due 2025-09-20
Leah Ortiz - upload sample workload traces and token distribution CSV to shared folder - due 2025-09-22
Priya Nair - draft benchmark plan (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost) - due 2025-09-21
summary: Kickoff scoping for a Private deployment POC. Primary constraints: strict egress rules, region-locked data residency (EU primary), requirement for VPC peering or PrivateLink, and SOC2-auditability of logs. Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, model accuracy regression limits), workload sizing (concurrent RPS, seq length distribution), and benchmark plan (2-week run on Dedicated capacity + canary). Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: POC success criteria and bench metrics
Workload sizing and KV cache behavior
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-18 14:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lucas Reed (Redwood), Dr. Harold Chen (Azalea CTO), Leah Ortiz (Azalea Head of ML), Marcus Liu (Cloud Infra), Tanya Reed (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Jordan on AE side, Priya our solutions engineer, Lucas on infra. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Harold: Hi all, Harold here. We're kicking off a POC to validate private networked inference for our clinical-support agent, data residency in EU, plus strict no-egress rules.
[00:22] Leah: Leah — we'll supply workload traces and would like to verify latency and cost targets; model accuracy must not regress more than 1% relative to our baseline.
[00:30] Marcus: Marcus, I own VPC and peering on our side, want to understand IP ranges, NAT/Egress flow, and PrivateLink options.
[00:36] Tanya: Tanya, security. SOC2 is in flight, need audit logs, KMS integration, and proof of auditability for the POC.
[00:44] Priya: Great. Agenda: align success criteria, define workload sizing, choose connectivity approach (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), discuss egress/firewall constraints and benchmarks/timeline.

[03:05] Jordan: To start success criteria — what are you measuring? Latency SLOs? Cost thresholds? Accuracy?
[03:12] Leah: Latency: 95th under 400ms for typical 256-token prompts, p99 under 750ms is ideal for user experience. Throughput: approx 60 concurrent requests during peak, average 15 rps sustained. Cost: we want ballpark for 1M tokens/month. Accuracy: less than 1% regression on our eval set.
[04:01] Priya: Helpful. We'll size a Dedicated pool for those numbers. Two quick follow-ups: sequence length distribution and prefix reuse (how much caching we can exploit).
[04:18] Leah: Distribution attached later, mostly 32-512 tokens, median ~128. We do use a lot of repeated prefixes for follow-ups.

[05:40] Marcus: On connectivity, our security policy prefers PrivateLink over classic VPC peering for tighter controls, but Peering may be simpler for cross-account routing. We also have region locks — all data must remain in eu-west-1.
[05:58] Priya: Right, both supported. Tradeoffs — VPC peering keeps traffic in the peered VPC and is straightforward for low-latency paths, PrivateLink avoids route table changes and supports endpoint policies. Peering requires CIDR planning. PrivateLink adds ENI overhead and sometimes NAT for egress.

[07:20] Jordan: Egress constraints — can you describe exactly what you mean by "no-egress"?
[07:26] Tanya: No customer data may leave eu-west-1. Egress to internet only through our approved proxies. Logs containing PII must be stored in our S3 in eu-west-1 with encryption keys under our KMS.
[07:40] Priya: For that case we recommend a Private deployment inside your VPC or a VPC peering with a Private Control Plane located in the EU. We can also do VPC peering and push logs to your S3 via a controlled VPC endpoint. We'll need to validate that audit logs and metrics never traverse outside the region.

[09:10] Leah: For the POC we prefer Redwood-managed runtime but inside our network boundary — either Dedicated in a dedicated tenant that peers to our VPC or Redwood Private with control plane in the EU.
[09:24] Lucas: Can you outline what Redwood needs from our side to set up peering? IP ranges, route tables, security groups? We have strict NACLs.
[09:34] Priya: We'll need a /24 from you for the peering interface, or we can implement PrivateLink with an endpoint service and you create an interface endpoint. Also security groups for the service ports (we'll share specifics). For the POC we'll provide an initial network diagram and a checklist.

[11:00] Marcus: What's the expected handshake for TLS and mTLS? Is there client cert support?
[11:06] Priya: We support mutual TLS for the Private control plane and TLS for data plane. For PrivateLink, the interface is inside your VPC and mutual TLS is optional but supported. KMS integration for encryption-at-rest and customer-managed keys via our KMS connector is possible.

[13:12] Jordan: Benchmarks — Priya, can you walk through the plan?
[13:17] Priya: Sure. Proposal: 2-week benchmark window on Dedicated capacity pinned to a specific model variant. Phase 1: warm-up + functional verification (2 days). Phase 2: steady-state throughput runs to measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec (5 days). Phase 3: regression tests for accuracy with the customer's eval set (2 days). Phase 4: stress tests for cache-eviction, long-tail seqs and burst traffic (4 days). We'll collect token cost, GPU utilization, and per-route latency breakdowns.
[14:05] Leah: For the accuracy tests we will supply a reproducible eval harness and baseline outputs.

[15:20] Marcus: For the steady-state runs what instance profiles are you planning? We need an estimate of GPU hours for budget approvals.
[15:28] Priya: For the specified load (~60 concurrent with median 128 tokens), our initial estimate is a 4-GPU Dedicated cluster (A100-class or similar), autoscaling disabled during bench to get deterministic metrics. That equates to roughly 48 GPU-hours/day; we'll refine after receiving the actual token distribution.

[17:00] Jordan: Customer wants cost per 1M tokens — can we give a ballpark?
[17:06] Priya: Ballpark: depending on batching and KV cache hit rates, anywhere from $4 to $12 per 1M tokens on Dedicated. With aggressive batching and prefix cache we can push toward the low end. We'll provide a model-based estimate once we have the distribution.

[18:30] Tanya: Audit logs and retention — we need to ensure log exports to our S3 with encryption, and an immutable audit trail for 90 days for the POC. Is that supported?
[18:40] Priya: Yes, Redwood can export request/response metadata and system traces to your S3 bucket in-region, and KMS keys can be customer-managed. We will redact full user prompt streams if you request to avoid sensitive PII exposure in logs.

[20:10] Lucas: Any minimum network throughput expectations? We have bursty usage and want to size ENIs and MTU.
[20:18] Priya: Expect ~50-200 Mbps sustained for 60 concurrent with 128 tokens, depending on response sizes and chunking. We'll include TCP windowing and MTU knobs in the network checklist.

[22:00] Harold: Timeline — we need a 3-week pilot window before end of Q4 to present to the board. Can we hit a POC start within 2 weeks?
[22:10] Jordan: Likely yes if we get network details and sample traces quickly. Typical lead time for provisioning Dedicated in-region is 5-10 business days, plus 2-3 days for networking coordination.

[23:50] Leah: For the POC success criteria — let's document them so we're aligned: 95th < 400ms, p99 < 750ms, cost under $8/1M tokens, no model regression >1%, all data residency in eu-west-1, logs accessible in our S3 w/ CMK.
[24:12] Priya: Noted. We'll add a couple of guardrails: KV cache hit rate target of >30% to achieve cost goals, and batching config to keep latency within SLO.

[26:00] Marcus: Network security checklist items — NACL entries, allowed ports, certs, and where to place a transit gateway if we use multiple AZs.
[26:12] Priya: We'll send a detailed checklist and a diagram. If you prefer PrivateLink we can document interface endpoint scaling and ENI limits across AZs.

[28:40] Tanya: About compliance docs — can you share SOC2 docs, penetration test summaries, and data flow diagrams?
[28:50] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the security pack, SOC2 Type II summary, and our standard penetration test report under an NDA link. We'll also include a mini whitepaper on audit log exports and KMS integration.

[30:20] Leah: A technical question — how does Redwood handle KV cache persistence across restarts? We saw during an internal test that cache miss storms can spike tokens.
[30:28] Priya: The runtime maintains in-memory KV cache per instance and a lightweight shared cache layer for warmup. For Dedicated we can tune checkpoint frequency and pre-warm with a cached prefix set during the bench to avoid cold starts. We'll run cache warm-up runs as part of Phase 1.

[33:10] Lucas: Can we pin model versions for the POC? We need deterministic behavior for evaluation.
[33:16] Priya: Yes, you can pin a model version and pin quantization profile. We'll also run canary deploys during the pilot if you want rolling updates, but for the bench we'll keep a fixed pinned variant.
transcript_continued:
[35:00] Jordan: One more on routing — if we do VPC peering, we need to confirm route table propagation and avoid overlapping CIDR. If PrivateLink, we'll need interface endpoints in each AZ.
[35:18] Marcus: Overlap will be an issue; we'll carve out a /24 for this POC.
[36:20] Priya: Great. Bench monitoring — we'll emit per-token cost, per-route p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and request attribution. We'll provide a dashboard link and raw CSVs.
[37:40] Leah: For accuracy regression tests, we will run our eval harness nightly and compare diffs. If regression >1% we fail the POC.
[38:00] Priya: We'll automate the eval run and provide regression alerts.
[39:15] Tanya: Do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for the console? We need role separation during the POC.
[39:22] Jordan: Yes, SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls are supported. We'll provide admin and read-only roles for your team.
[40:30] Marcus: Egress to internal proxies — we will force all outbound through a NAT/proxy. Can Redwood accommodate that?
[40:36] Priya: Yes, you can route from the service subnets through your egress proxies. We'll validate with a short connectivity test.
[41:55] Jordan: Pricing note — Dedicated POC pricing usually includes a short-term reserved capacity plus usage for bench runs. I'll include an estimate in the packet.
[42:10] Leah: If Dedicated costs are too high, could we consider a hybrid — some workloads on Dedicated (hot path) and lower critical on hosted?
[42:20] Priya: Hybrid is possible but for strict residency we'd still need the data plane in-region. We can explore routing lower-sensitivity traffic to hosted endpoints if allowed.
[44:00] Harold: Risk discussion — what are biggest failure modes during POC?
[44:06] Priya: Networking misconfigurations, cold cache causing high cost/latency, and model mismatches. We mitigate with a checklist, pre-warm steps, and pinned variants.
[45:30] Jordan: Any legal/procurement blockers we should flag early?
[45:36] Tanya: We'll need a data processing addendum and clarifications on liability. Our legal is ready to review once we see the T&Cs and DPA.
[46:10] Jordan: We'll fast-track the DPA and include the security pack.
[47:00] Priya: Operational runbooks — for failover we can suggest a canary fallback to a smaller model in another region if capacity is constrained, but that may violate residency requirements.
[47:20] Marcus: We can't cross-region for production data; fallback must be to an in-region variant.
[48:00] Leah: Let's recap the committed next steps.
[48:06] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send network diagram, PrivateLink vs peering checklist, security pack, and benchmark plan. Azalea to share token distribution and eval harness. Schedule bench window in ~2 weeks pending provisioning.
[49:10] Leah: Agreed. Also please specify the exact ports and ENI counts per AZ.
[49:22] Priya: Will do.
[50:00] Harold: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the demo and benchmark results.
[50:06] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up by end of day with the packet.
[50:12] Meeting ended.
